value:
CENSUS EXTENSION AND PARTIAL REFUTATION of claim.law.addr16-lo-home-copy-census-no-source-discriminant.20260831.v1 (the AD census). Three findings, all measured image-wide over 2983 paired functions.

FINDING 1 - THE CLASS IS 40 FUNCTIONS, NOT 24, AND IT SWALLOWS TWO OF THE FIVE 'DIFFERENT MECHANISM' PARKS. AD's FINDING 6 censused the home copy only where the intermediate is r0 and the copy is spelled `mr rHOME,r0`, and on that basis reported T=0/O=0 for world/items::LoadItems, world/world::StartWorldLoad, ui/select::init_player_change, pb/pb_objregs::pbDrawVerts and enemy/critter::ProcessCritterList, concluding all five are a different mechanism outside the class. Generalising the intermediate to ANY volatile and the copy to `addi rHOME,rX,0 | mr rHOME,rX` (tools/gdl/addrlo_home_general_census.py) gives, per (function, callee-saved register receiving a file-scope address): shape A `lis rT,SYM@ha ; addi rHOME,rT,SYM@lo` (direct home) target 920 / ours 887; shape B (copy paid) target 33 / ours 75. Per-function populations paired on the shape-B count: P (ours more copies) = 40, Q (equal, nonzero) = 24, R (both zero) = 2919, S (ours FEWER copies) = 0. The P roster CONTAINS all 24 of AD's instances plus 16 more, INCLUDING LoadItems and StartWorldLoad. Those two are therefore NOT a different mechanism: they are the same ADDR16_LO home copy, merely routed through a general volatile (r3 and r5 respectively) and spelled `addi r30,rX,0` instead of `mr r30,r0`. AD's do-not-probe disposition DOES extend to them. The other three (init_player_change, pbDrawVerts, ProcessCritterList) really are outside the class (tB=0, oB=0 on all three) and are handled separately.

FINDING 2 - S = 0 SURVIVES THE GENERALISATION, OVER 953 OPPORTUNITIES. The one-directionality that AD used to argue allocator-internal causation is not an artifact of the r0-only filter: with the general intermediate there are still zero functions where the target pays a home copy our build avoids. Failure rate 40/2983 functions, 75 vs 33 instances.

FINDING 3 - THE PROLOGUE-SHADOW AXIS IS NOT DEAD; AD'S C4 USED THE WRONG STATISTIC. AD falsified the shadow hypothesis on the AGGREGATE histogram ('near-identical, both cap at 4 hoisted, only 34/2983 functions disagree'). The conditional statistic is decisive and points the other way. Of those same 34 shadow-size disagreements, 28 are ours-larger, and 21 of those 28 are exactly the P functions whose surplus copy lands IN the shadow - a 2x2 of (ours-hoists-MORE x shape-B surplus) = 21 / 7 / 19 / 2103. P-shadow functions are 21 of 2150 framed functions (1%) but 62% of every shadow-size disagreement in the image. Instance-level: TARGET shape-A in shadow 0/920 and OURS shape-A in shadow 0/887 (structural - a callee-saved home cannot be written before the stmw), TARGET shape-B in shadow 2/33, OURS shape-B in shadow 29/75. Reading the 21 shadow rosters directly, the target's prologue shadow contains the `lis SYM@ha` ALONE in every one of the 21, while ours contains the `lis` PLUS the low-half `addi`. So over-hoisting and the home copy are ONE event, not two independent ones. This does not overturn AD's verdict - it renames it. The mechanism is not 'the allocator declined to coalesce and the scheduler then hoisted the now-volatile addi'; it is a single joint decision whose two halves are observationally inseparable, and the surplus is exactly one instruction of prologue-shadow fill. NO SOURCE LEVER FOLLOWS: probed on LoadItems (see attempt.loaditems-addrlo-home-copy-cap.20260901.v1) and the axis is unavailable from source.

DISPOSITION. Treat LoadItems and StartWorldLoad as P-class: a known, named, accepted one-instruction residual; finish their bodies on their own merits. Per claim.law.webfrank-cannot-close-a-count-asymmetric-residual.20260831.v1 the whole class remains WebFrank-ineligible (ours is exactly one instruction longer).
